title: Why does select give 99 files, not 4?
fullTitle: FFmpeg select Keyframes: 99 Files, 4 Different, Fixed by -fps_mode vfr

scenes.narration: You select the keyframes of a clip with select equals e q, pict type, I. You expect four files. You get ninety nine. Is select broken? A synthetic clip, a keyframe every second, every output file hashed, on f f m peg six point one point one.

The clip: a hundred frames, each with its own gray level. Keyframes at zero, twenty five, fifty and seventy five. Reader one hashes every file written. Reader two is f f m peg's own frame md five and its dup counter. Control: no select gives a hundred files, a hundred different hashes.

Default output: ninety nine files. Four different hashes. Ninety five duplicates. The runs: twenty four, twenty five, twenty five, twenty five. Select did its job. Only keyframes come out. The duplicates come after it.

Add dash fps mode vfr: four files, no duplicates. Dash fps mode passthrough: four. Dash vsync zero: four. Dash vsync vfr: four. Explicit dash fps mode cfr: ninety nine again. Dash skip frame nokey on the input: ninety nine. Resetting timestamps with set p t s: four.

Why: an image sequence is written at a constant frame rate, and select leaves holes in the timeline. Each hole is filled by repeating the previous frame. Keyframes at zero, ten, forty, forty one: fifty files, runs of nine, thirty, two, nine. The output stops after the last repeat, not at the end of the clip.
captions: Holes in the timeline are filled by repeats.

scenes.narration: Same story in a video. M P four, default: ninety nine frames, three point nine six seconds. With dash fps mode vfr: four frames, three point zero four seconds. The rule: select, then dash fps mode vfr.
Select keyframes, add dash fps mode vfr, count the files. Not tested: other muxers, variable frame rate input, real footage, and builds other than six point one point one.
captions: Not tested: other builds, real footage.
